frank.feedback: Loop-of-loops is representable as typed recurrent state/runtime semantics in the tested proxy; no FRANK-specific ClayCode core primitive is justified.

clayresearch.feedback: BASE_CLAYCODE_RELEASE remains the active gate; prioritize compiler/runtime realization over semantic redesign.

claygraph.feedback: Loop coupling must preserve typed hyperrelation roles, epochs, selection/projection receipts and graph!=authority boundaries.

unifieddb.feedback: Loop state, scheduler decisions and execution receipts require revisioned identities and replayable state; runtime loop identity must not collapse work/resource/capability identity.

gwt.feedback: Recurrence remains distinct from emergence; loop control must consume typed outcome/re-entry evidence rather than an emergence scalar.

hyperposition.feedback: Multirate recurrent coupling should retain gain/delay/timescale and higher-order topology as typed state rather than flattening to pairwise scalar edges.

emergenz.feedback: Convergence, productive cycles, stagnation and divergence are dynamics classes, not emergence claims; lesion/rescue and shuffled controls remain required for causal promotion.

harness.feedback: No H1/H2/H3 gate advances. The loop runtime candidate should later be differential-tested against frozen H1 loop traces on Ubuntu.

inputs: prior typed-canonical, namespace and control-flow trigger runs
claycode.feedback: Keep current semantic core. Add/freeze loop-network schemas and runtime lowering only after production tests; reuse the already identified general structured-control-flow work rather than inventing FRANK-specific loop syntax.
